clue.text: Anna's employer's present cause of ruin

definitions.meaning: Anna Leonowens worked for the King of Siam, whose gift of a sacred pale beast was costly to keep
a possession whose upkeep beggars its owner

explanation.surface: A governess receives a gift from her boss that will bankrupt her.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna is the governess of The King and I; the King of Siam was said to give courtiers sacred albino animals whose keep ruined them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a burdensome gift, from the Siamese royal custom, and by extension any costly, useless possession.

clue.text: Man from India shows where rabbits proliferate on port

indicators.note: on means in this down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a warren is a network of rabbit burrows
Hastings is a port town on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: An Indian man points out where rabbits breed on a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: He was the first Governor-General of British India, impeached on his return.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Governor-General of Bengal, a figure famous for his career in British India.

clue.text: Pub, The Queen, next to The Bull

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Pubs named The Queen and The Bull stand side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' looks like another pub; it is the bullseye of a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard or target the ring just outside the central bullseye.

clue.text: Tennyson's hero is one up on daily study

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word one is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman, a char
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: The poet's protagonist is a step ahead on his everyday studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ONE into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of a narrative poem by the Victorian Poet Laureate, a sailor who returns home after years away.

clue.text: One spotted lying down with Isaiah's kid

definitions.meaning: a big cat with a dappled coat
Isaiah 11:6 prophesies that this animal shall lie down with the young goat

explanation.surface: Someone noticed reclining beside the prophet's child.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted big cat appears in Isaiah's vision of peace alongside the young goat.

clue.text: Stick you are said to get from the chemist

parts.note: paste is glue for sticking

indicators.note: said means the words you are are spoken, giving a sound written with two letters

parts.note: the two words spoken quickly

explanation.surface: You can buy glue at the pharmacy, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the chemist' looks like a pharmacy; it is the French scientist Louis Pasteur.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a French scientist who devised pasteurisation and early vaccines.

clue.text: Where sermons were delivered, both classical

definitions.meaning: an early church pulpit or reading desk

explanation.surface: A pulpit for preaching sermons in old times, both ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised desk in early Christian churches for reading and preaching, and Latin for 'the pair'.

clue.text: Old character gets account for a bird

parts.note: thorn is an Old English runic letter
a bill is an account to be paid

explanation.surface: An elderly eccentric receives a bill for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests an eccentric person; it is an old letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Australian songbird of the warbler family.

clue.text: Extension 101 for these resorts?

parts.note: 101 is CI in Roman numerals, the abbreviation that these islands extend to their full name

explanation.surface: A phone extension number for a holiday booking line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extension 101' looks like a telephone line; CI spelt out in full is the name of the islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey, Guernsey and their neighbours are holiday islands whose abbreviation is CI.

clue.text: Gunner sergeant for instance uncommonly sour and spiteful

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, gives a gunner
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the word sour is arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: An artillery sergeant who is unusually bitter and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunner' looks like the subject of the sentence; it only gives the Royal Artillery. 'uncommonly' rearranges SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness, so a rancorous person is malicious and full of ill will.

clue.text: Soup associated with a fine Irish boy

definitions.meaning: a thin liquid dish of stock and vegetables

definitions.text: associated with a fine Irish boy
definitions.meaning: the Irish phrase 'a — of a boy' praises a lively, splendid lad

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup linked to a handsome lad from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thin stock-based dish, and also the word in the Irish idiom praising a spirited young fellow.

clue.text: High cost of our transport through space

definitions.meaning: as in 'it cost the —', an enormous price
the planet that carries us all round the sun

explanation.surface: A space journey for all of us comes at a steep price.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'cost the world' style phrase uses the planet for a huge price, and the planet itself is our vehicle through the cosmos.

clue.text: Copy PM's address to summit

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
the Prime Minister lives at Number 10 Downing Street, and 10 in Roman numerals is X

explanation.surface: Someone copies the Prime Minister's speech for a top-level meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a speech; it is the PM's house number, Ten, as the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The top point or peak of something, the highest part.

clue.text: One in the chapter without chapter heading, or name, presently

indicators.note: without means the following letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a canon is one of the clergy who make up a cathedral chapter

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the second word chapter is used

explanation.surface: A clergyman in the chapter, without a heading or name, will appear soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or name' adds a second hint: the short form of anonymous means having no name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for soon or shortly, meaning in a little while.

clue.text: Crazy type liable to such happy (if non-U) changes

indicators.note: liable says the following words are apt to be rearranged, part of the shuffling signal with changes
changes means the words to such happy, minus the letter excluded, are rearranged

parts.note: non-U names the letter U as the one that is not in the answer, so it is taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A madman is likely to change a happy situation.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is also a pun: British slang for not upper-class, so the 'happy' type is liable to lose his manners. 'changes' rearranges TO SUCH HAPPY once the U is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a severe personality disorder, colloquially a madman.

clue.text: County subdivision, a Chiltern one perhaps

definitions.meaning: an old English administrative division of a shire
the Chiltern ... is a nominal office MPs take in order to resign their seats

explanation.surface: A district of a county, such as one in the Chiltern Hills.
explanation.walkthrough: An English MP cannot simply resign, so takes the sinecure of Steward of the Chiltern Hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: An old administrative division of an English shire, also the number one more than ninety-nine.

clue.text: Coinage of monies possibly holding the record

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled monies goes around the record
possibly suggests monies may be arranged another way

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Minting coins may involve keeping the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' looks like minted money, matching 'monies'; it means a new word. 'possibly' rearranges MONIES into NEOISM, and 'holding' puts the record inside after NEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented word or expression.

clue.text: Breathing-space in which various peers consume it

indicators.note: consume means the peers take the word it inside them
various suggests the letters of peers are taken in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pause in which assorted lords eat something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consume' looks like eating; it is the container signal. 'various' rearranges PEERS into RESPE, which takes IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A short break or rest from effort or difficulty.

clue.text: Debtor, outwardly diffident, appears a bit wet

indicators.note: outwardly means the shy word sits on the outside, around the debtor

parts.note: a diffident person is shy
a debtor is one who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: A shy debtor seems a little drippy.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with brief spells of rain is slightly damp.

clue.text: Element shows young Tory leaders not half triumphant

indicators.note: leaders points to the first letters of young and Tory
not half means only the front half of the word triumphant

explanation.surface: Young Conservative leaders display muted triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' (British slang for 'very much') takes TRIUM, the first five of ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare-earth metallic chemical element, number 39.

clue.text: Proposed law about a hundred and one micro-organisms

indicators.note: about means the bill goes around the following letters

parts.note: a bill is a draft law before Parliament
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A draft law on a hundred and one kinds of germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and C inside BILL, giving BACILL, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod-shaped bacteria, tiny living things seen only under a microscope.

clue.text: Heater for a metal-worker

definitions.meaning: a pan of burning coals for warmth

explanation.surface: A heater made for a smith.
explanation.definitionFit: A charcoal pan for heating, and a craftsman in brass.

clue.text: Trickster explains his image

parts.note: the trickster refers to himself as I
a con is short for a con man, a swindler

explanation.surface: A swindler explains his reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The trickster's explanation is the boast 'I con'.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or likeness, especially a sacred painting in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Scene of eruption in Vietnam

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the word Vietnam

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts somewhere in south-east Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The volcano is in Sicily, not Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is famous for frequent outbursts of lava.

clue.text: Not on a half-century? Rubbish!

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman scores no fifty: what a load of nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-century' suggests cricket, fifty runs; here just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal entrails or waste parts, by extension worthless stuff.

clue.text: Runs from the Egyptian plague

definitions.meaning: one of the ten plagues of Egypt in Exodus was swarms of these insects

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from a disease in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to dash along, and swarms of insects were sent upon Pharaoh's land.

clue.text: Tendency of grass to be crooked

definitions.meaning: a stiff wiry type of grass

explanation.surface: Grass tends to grow at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclination or flair, a wiry meadow plant, and twisted or corrupt.

clue.text: Forbidding the last of the dirt

parts.note: a forbidding look is grim

indicators.note: the last of points to the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: The final bit of muck looks unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrained soot or filth on a surface.

clue.text: Modern impressionist art

parts.note: not a school of painting but the skill of a mimic doing impressions

explanation.surface: A gallery label for contemporary paintings in the style of Monet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressionist' suggests Monet; it is the comedian who mimics voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is the impersonator's craft, copying others' manner.

clue.text: As to home perms — transformations!

indicators.note: transformations signals that the letters of the preceding words change shape

explanation.surface: Home hair perms bring about dramatic changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid's poem title and the general word for changes of form.
